note: Expected parse results for stream.h264. Every hop that classifies NAL types asserts against this. `nals` are nal_unit_type values in order.

cases.name: keyframe-au-4byte
cases.note: Canonical keyframe access unit, 4-byte start codes: AUD, SPS, PPS, IDR.

cases.name: delta-au-4byte
cases.note: Ordinary delta access unit. The steady-state case.

cases.name: delta-au-3byte-startcodes
cases.note: Same shape with 3-byte start codes. A parser hardcoded to 4 bytes misses every NAL here.

cases.name: delta-au-mixed-startcodes
cases.note: 4-byte AUD then 3-byte slice. ffmpeg emits both widths; a parser must accept either mid-stream.

cases.name: keyframe-au-with-sei
cases.note: AUD, SPS, PPS, SEI, IDR — the real encoder's usual keyframe ordering.

cases.name: au-with-emulation-prevention
cases.note: Slice body contains 00 00 03 twice. Must yield exactly two NALs — a parser that reads 00 00 03 as a start code reports more.

cases.name: idr-without-parameter-sets
cases.note: IDR with no preceding SPS/PPS. A decoder cannot start here; the client gate treats this as a forced redial.

cases.name: parameter-sets-without-idr
cases.note: SPS+PPS with no slice. Carries no picture; must not be counted as a keyframe.

cases.name: no-nal-at-all
cases.note: Payload with no start code. The client counts this as `unparsed`; every hop must count it as perr and must not crash.
